verdict.rationale: PayPal's ACP/UCP flows use single-use, merchant-bound, time/amount-restricted tokens generated per checkout session (i.e., a de-facto per-purchase authorization token), and the agent toolkit docs explicitly recommend 'keep human oversight' for judgment-sensitive tasks, suggesting some consent-oriented design. However, no evidence describes an explicit user-facing confirmation/approval UI, a signed mandate artifact, or a required buyer sign-off step distinct from the underlying tokenized transaction mechanics — the docs describe the payment rails, not a consent UX. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of a user confirmation screen or mandate-signing step, evidence that spending requires active buyer approval beyond the checkout session itself, and any hands-on/independent report confirming this consent step in practice.
